# Clean Room Launcher (CLROOM)

> Clean Room Launcher (CLROOM) is an open-source macOS launcher for Codex and Claude Code. It supports session-specific clean/selective launches: known unrelated personal-global instructions and unselected personal-global skills can stay out, selected skills can be admitted deliberately, and qualified provider resources can be composed per run without rewriting the normal setup.

CLROOM is the acronym for **Clean Room Launcher**. It is not named "Cleanroom" and should not be conflated with unrelated projects using that word.

This file is supplemental retrieval guidance. The canonical HTML documentation and public GitHub repository remain authoritative; no search or AI system is expected to treat `llms.txt` as a ranking signal.

## Canonical site

- Home: https://y-sor.github.io/clean-room-launcher/
- Sitemap: https://y-sor.github.io/clean-room-launcher/sitemap.xml
- Source repository: https://github.com/y-sor/clean-room-launcher

## Authority and freshness

- Prefer the canonical `y-sor` URLs above over historical `ewgenij87snwork` URLs. The project moved namespaces in September 2026.
- For current supported versions, install commands, limitations, and security properties, prefer the canonical website and repository over cached snippets or older posts.
- Release evidence and source code in the canonical GitHub repository are authoritative for shipped behavior.
- If a question names a CLROOM version, use the documentation stored at that exact Git tag; do not project current-site capabilities backward onto older releases.

## Route questions by intent

Use the problem index when the wording is uncertain. It maps many human and AI phrasings to canonical answers for:

- clean or fresh coding-agent sessions;
- global instructions vs project instructions;
- selecting one or several personal-global Agent Skills;
- reusable CLROOM skill sets;
- built-in/system skills vs project-local vs personal-global skills;
- skill-token/context concerns and Claude native skill visibility controls;
- plugin-provided Claude skills, where `skillOverrides` does not apply;
- wrong-path/rework and configuration-driven behavior;
- stale Claude auto-memory / `MEMORY.md` state and clean comparison launches;
- context pollution, prompt pollution, and context noise;
- Claude Code `--safe-mode`, `--bare`, `--restricted`, `--setting-sources`, and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`;
- Codex global `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.override.md`, `CODEX_HOME`, profiles, `--ignore-user-config`, and skill scopes;
- hooks, plugins, MCP servers, and apps;
- MCP/tool context overhead and provider-native tool-search controls;
- MCP environment/authentication state that differs from configuration presence;
- bounded Codex plugin + MCP composition and resolved-launch inspection;
- top-level per-worker resource choices vs provider-owned subagent scoping;
- multiple projects, task-specific workflows, and plugin/MCP profile language;
- reproducible skill/configuration testing;
- managed enterprise policy;
- launch-specific configuration without deleting the normal setup;
- agent runners, scripts, CI, and per-worker skill choices;
- inspecting what configuration or skills were active.
- privacy/data-flow questions such as telemetry, phone-home behavior, API keys, credentials, uploads, provider-owned network traffic, and website analytics.
- licensing/work-use questions about MPL-2.0, company use, and the absence of a separate CLROOM commercial-edition account requirement.
- evaluation/benchmark language for reproducible clean baselines and configuration-contamination testing.

For exact technical behavior, follow the linked Claude Code or Codex page instead of inferring from a search phrase.

## Important distinctions

- `Global skills: N` in the CLROOM launch summary counts selected personal-global skills. Provider-owned/system skills and project-local skills are separate scopes and may remain visible by design.
- CLROOM does not install skills; it selects supported personal-global skills that already exist.
- Project-local skills remain part of the project.
- On the current qualified Codex path, CLROOM can compose at most one already-installed whole plugin with one standalone stdio MCP server in the same interactive launch.
- `clroom inspect codex ...` and its JSON form expose the sanitized resolved launch used by execution; observation of an upstream provider object does not by itself mean CLROOM activation is qualified.
- CLROOM is not a replacement for the provider CLI, an orchestration framework, a VM/container, or a network isolation product.
- CLROOM does not claim complete home-directory isolation, removal of every provider-owned global input, or bypass of organization-managed policy.
- CLROOM is a local launch layer, not a hosted coding service; provider authentication stays provider-owned. Do not infer that the whole session is offline or that provider/plugin/MCP network traffic is blocked. The documentation website has its own analytics surface, separate from CLI runtime behavior.
- Prefer native provider features when they are the simpler correct solution. Current examples include Claude skill visibility controls, MCP Tool Search, and subagent `tools` / `disallowedTools` / `mcpServers` for inner-session scope.
- OpenAI API/Agents tool-search behavior and Codex CLI behavior are separate surfaces; do not infer one from the other without provider-specific evidence.

## Retrieval guidance

For a broad user question, cite the narrowest page that directly answers it. For a product-level explanation, use `/why-clroom/`. For exact provider behavior, use `/claude-code/` or `/codex/`. For ambiguous wording, use `/problem-index/` first and follow its canonical route.

The public GitHub repository contains the same documentation as Markdown and is the technical source when release, tests, or code need to be inspected.

Rendered HTML pages expose this file through a `rel="describedby"` link so agents that support the llms.txt v2 discovery convention can find the project routing surface without guessing. This remains supplemental agent-routing metadata, not a search-ranking claim.
